news.snippet: 2026年Q1录得2887起AI融资，显示行业回暖，AI企业估值倍数成为市场关注焦点，并影响投资定价逻辑。
news.raw_snippet:
Q1 2026 recorded 2,887 AI funding rounds, signaling the recovery may not a one-off. Late-reported deals may push the number higher. Whether 2026 sets another record will depend on later-stage activity and the long-awaited IPOs of frontier AI labs.

## Deal volumes by funding stage: AI’s formative era

Right now, investors are still getting accustomed to the rising interest in new startups focused on applications of Artificial Intelligence. [...] In 2015, there were over 2,000 funding rounds in the Artificial Intelligence sector. That is a significant number as Artificial Intelligence as a theme has been around for decades but still remained dwarfed by other investing themes of the past years, such as SaaS. The interest and funding has been growing at a rapid pace since 2015.

AI Valuations: Number of funding rounds [...] After three years of decline, AI funding rounds jumped 50% in 2025 to a new high of 7,646, beating the 2021 peak. The rebound was driven by stronger investor conviction, the rise of agentic AI and enterprise use cases, and a broader recovery in venture capital. Unlike 2021, when capital flooded all of tech, the 2025 surge was focused on AI.

news.title: Palo Alto Networks斥资45亿美元收购Applied Compute，押注企业AI
news.snippet: 该收购将为网络安全公司提供AI算力技术，助力Palo Alto Networks强化企业级AI安全解决方案与竞争力。
news.raw_snippet:
## The deal will give the cybersecurity company technology to train, customize, and deploy open-weight AI models

Palo Alto Networks has agreed to buy Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion, a move the company said will let it train, deploy and secure open-weight AI models for enterprises in the public cloud or in their own sovereign environments. [...] “The acquisition will bring Applied Compute’s platform and world-class AI research team to Palo Alto Networks to help enterprises adopt AI securely, whether they choose open-weight models, closed frontier models, or both,” the company said in a statement released alongside its fiscal first quarter 2027 results. The statement described Applied Compute as “a leading platform for post-training and inference of open-weight AI models” and said the startup will continue to serve AI-native companies, [...] The transaction is expected to close in Palo Alto’s fiscal third quarter of 2027, which runs from February to April, the statement said. Applied Compute co-founder and CEO Yash Patil will become Palo Alto’s co-chief AI officer, and the startup’s research team will help build AI models across the company’s offerings.
